precepts.text: And after this I beheld, and lo, there was gathered together a multitude of men, out of number, from the four winds of the heaven, to subdue the man that came out of the sea. So the winds are the armies of the earth. The winds are the armies of the earth, sent to subdue the man, also sent to bring destruction on this earth.
precepts.point: What is the wind that is going to blow on the earth? This cannot be a normal wind. It is windy every day. It is windy every single day. This is a different type of wind that is mentioned here in Revelation.

note.label: Unity: The Sweet Savor Of Salvation

precepts.why:
Four angels stand on the four corners of the earth, “holding the four winds of the earth, that the wind should not blow on the earth, nor on the sea”. So what is the wind that is going to blow on the earth? It cannot be a normal wind. It is windy every single day. This is a different type of wind.

Ezra shows it: “And after this I beheld, and, lo, there was gathered together a multitude of men, out of number, from the four winds of the heaven, to subdue the man that came out of the sea.” So the winds are the armies of the earth, gathered to subdue the man that came out of the sea, and sent to bring destruction on this earth.

Then the angel with the seal of the living God cries to the four angels, “Hurt not the earth, neither the sea, nor the trees, till we have sealed the servants of our God in their foreheads.” The armies are held back; no destruction of mass proportions is coming until the hundred and forty and four thousand are sealed, and that seal is the law.

So if you truly want the end to come, you are going to be out here teaching your people and raising up the nation of Israel. The Most High God is waiting on a specific number, 144,000 unified in keeping the commandments and the faith of Christ, and then deliverance will come. The Christian church never even talks about the 144,000, because it is not about the deliverance of our people. Unity is the sweet savor of salvation.

precepts.text: A multitude of men, out of number, from the four winds of the heaven, to subdue the man that came out of the sea. That's their military.
precepts.point: And there were sealed an hundred and forty and four thousand of all the tribes of the children of Israel: these are the leaders here; 144,000 is just the leading men. In order for them to be sealed, they got to know who they are, at least to some extent. So how you going to read that and be confused about the 12 tribes? You just read all of the tribes there. You can't make this stuff up.

note.label: Raising Up the Tabernacle of David That Fell

precepts.why:
Four angels hold the four winds of the earth, and another angel cries to them, “Hurt not the earth, neither the sea, nor the trees, till we have sealed the servants of our God in their foreheads.” The four winds are held back for a reason, and Ezra shows what gathers from those four winds.

“And after this I beheld, and, lo, there was gathered together a multitude of men, out of number, from the four winds of the heaven, to subdue the man that came out of the sea.” That multitude out of number is their military, gathered from the four winds to fight against Christ, the man that came out of the sea.

So the holding of the winds is this: do not let war pop off to the max until the servants of God are sealed. The armies of the nations are held back until the leaders of Israel, the hundred and forty and four thousand of all the tribes, are sealed with the law of God in Christ.

precepts.text: Bind up the testimony, seal the law among my disciples. That's the seal of the living God.
precepts.point: And there were sealed an hundred and forty and four thousand of all the tribes of the children of Israel: these are the leaders here; 144,000 is just the leading men. In order for them to be sealed, they got to know who they are, at least to some extent. So how you going to read that and be confused about the 12 tribes? You just read all of the tribes there. You can't make this stuff up.

note.label: Raising Up the Tabernacle of David That Fell

precepts.why:
The angel ascending from the east has “the seal of the living God”, and the servants of our God are sealed in their foreheads. What is that seal? Isaiah says it: “Bind up the testimony, seal the law among my disciples.” That is the seal of the living God: the law, sealed among his disciples, in Christ.

And the ones sealed are “an hundred and forty and four thousand of all the tribes of the children of Israel”, twelve thousand of every tribe, from Juda to Benjamin. These are the leaders; the 144,000 is just the leading men. In order for them to be sealed, they have to know who they are, at least to some extent.

So how are you going to read that and be confused about the twelve tribes? You just read all of the tribes right there. You can't make this stuff up.

precepts.text: Hurt not the earth, neither the sea, nor the trees, till we have sealed the servants of our God in their foreheads. And there were sealed an hundred and forty and four thousand of all the tribes of the children of Israel. What is the seal? Go right back to Isaiah 8:16: the law, in the forehead, in the mind.
precepts.point: The Song of Solomon is a metaphor: the whole book represents the Lord's relationship with his chosen people Israel. Set me as a seal upon thine heart, as a seal upon thine arm. The heart is the mind. What is the seal? The law, the words of God.

note.label: 250 Years of Celebration 400 Years of Sweat Equity (Pt 2)

precepts.why:
“And I heard the number of them which were sealed: and there were sealed an hundred and forty and four thousand of all the tribes of the children of Israel.” Then jump up to verse 3: “Hurt not the earth, neither the sea, nor the trees, till we have sealed the servants of our God in their foreheads.”

What is the seal talking about? Go right back to Isaiah 8:16: “Bind up the testimony, seal the law among my disciples.” The servants of God are sealed in their foreheads with the law, the same place Deuteronomy said the words of God would be “as frontlets between your eyes”, in the mind. Some are still saying the star of Moloch, the star of David; that is simple.

So the seal of Song of Solomon 8:6, set upon the heart and upon the arm, is the seal of the servants of God in Revelation: the law, laid up in the mind of the tribes of the children of Israel.

precepts.text: There were sealed 144,000 of all the tribes of the children of Israel. Manasseh is mentioned by name, and of the tribe of Joseph were sealed 12,000: Joseph here is Ephraim.
precepts.point: Cornelius was a centurion of the Italian band, a devout man that feared God with all his house. Where was he from? Caesarea. On the map, Caesarea sits right above Samaria: that's Manasseh's land. Cornelius was northern kingdom, not a Gentile of the nations. Do some research; do some study.

note.label: Joseph in Egypt: Then & Now

precepts.why:
“And I heard the number of them which were sealed: and there were sealed an hundred and forty and four thousand of all the tribes of the children of Israel.” All the tribes, the northern kingdom along with the southern, are sealed. The two kingdoms that God said he would bring back together are there together in the end.

Look at the bottom of verse 6: “Of the tribe of Manasses were sealed twelve thousand.” Manasseh is mentioned by name, the same tribe whose land Caesarea sat in, where Cornelius came from.

Then verse 8: “Of the tribe of Joseph were sealed twelve thousand.” Highlight that. Joseph is mentioned, and Ephraim is not. Joseph here is Ephraim.

So the northern kingdom that Christians say disappeared is sealed in Revelation 7, Manasseh by his own name and Ephraim under the name of Joseph. That is the tabernacle of David built again: all twelve tribes counted and sealed.

precepts.text: Four angels hold the four winds, the armies on land, sea and air, until the servants of God are sealed in their foreheads; the seal is the law bound among the disciples, not the hexagram, and the sealed are the 144,000 of all the tribes of the children of Israel.
precepts.point: He that endures to the end shall be saved. This gospel of the kingdom shall be preached in all the world for a witness, and then shall the end come: that world is the 144,000, and when they are sealed the end comes.

note.label: From Exile & Tribulation to Promise

precepts.why:
“And this gospel of the kingdom shall be preached in all the world for a witness unto all nations; and then shall the end come.” Earlier Christ said in Matthew 10, “Ye shall not have gone over the cities of Israel, till the Son of man be come.” So we are not going to reach all the Israelites. Then what does “all the world” mean, and when does the end come? Revelation 7 answers.

“I saw four angels standing on the four corners of the earth, holding the four winds of the earth”. That is the fighting, the wars. “That the wind should not blow on the earth”: the armies. “Nor on the sea”: the marines and the navies. “Nor on any tree”: what is above the trees is the air force.

“And I saw another angel ascending from the east, having the seal of the living God”. The seal of the living God is not the hexagram. It is the law: “Bind up the testimony, seal the law among my disciples.” He cried to the four angels “to whom it was given to hurt the earth and the sea”, hurt it with destruction: “Hurt not the earth, neither the sea, nor the trees, till we have sealed the servants of our God in their foreheads.”

“And there were sealed an hundred and forty and four thousand of all the tribes of the children of Israel.” So the end begins when the 144,000 are sealed. The world Christ is talking about in Matthew 24 is the 144,000: when they are sealed, then shall the end come.

precepts.text: The number of the children of Israel shall be as the sand of the sea which cannot be numbered, and where it was said ye are not my people they shall be called the sons of the living God.
precepts.point: These are they which came out of great tribulation and washed their robes white in the blood of the Lamb: so much for not going through tribulation.

note.label: From Exile & Tribulation to Promise

precepts.why:
“After this I beheld, and, lo, a great multitude, which no man could number”. Now that we are bringing this out, the churches say we are all included, all backgrounds and cultures together. Where was that in 1964? Where was it on the slave ships? That is why the Bible says precept must be upon precept, line upon line, here a little and there a little.

Hosea 1:10: “Yet the number of the children of Israel shall be as the sand of the sea, which cannot be measured nor numbered”. That is us. The multitude “which no man could number” is the children of Israel, whose number cannot be measured nor numbered.

“And it shall come to pass, that in the place where it was said unto them, Ye are not my people, there it shall be said unto them, Ye are the sons of the living God.” The people told they were not God’s people are the same ones called the sons of the living God.

It also shows time has gone by. Moses said “ye shall be left few in number among the heathen”, because they were killing us; Hosea says we would grow to be like the sand of the sea. That is the great multitude standing before the throne.

precepts.text: Jews, devout men, out of every nation under heaven: the all nations of Revelation 7:9.
precepts.point: These are they which came out of great tribulation and washed their robes white in the blood of the Lamb: so much for not going through tribulation.

note.label: From Exile & Tribulation to Promise

precepts.why:
The great multitude is “of all nations, and kindreds, and people, and tongues”, and the Christian says, see, we are all included. But read Acts 2:5: “And there were dwelling at Jerusalem Jews, devout men, out of every nation under heaven.”

Out of every nation under heaven, and they were Jews. So “all nations” in Revelation 7:9 does not mean every race; it means the Israelites scattered into every nation, gathered out of them.

That is the all nations of Revelation 7:9: Jews out of every nation under heaven, the same people as the sand of the sea that cannot be numbered, standing before the throne and before the Lamb.

precepts.text: The Lord sets his hand the second time, the first being under Moses, to recover the remnant from Assyria, Egypt, Pathros, Cush, Elam, Shinar, Hamath and the islands of the sea, and gathers the outcasts of Israel and the dispersed of Judah from the four corners of the earth.
precepts.point: These are they which came out of great tribulation and washed their robes white in the blood of the Lamb: so much for not going through tribulation.

note.label: From Exile & Tribulation to Promise

precepts.why:
If you have time on the street, add Isaiah 11: “the Lord shall set his hand again the second time to recover the remnant of his people”. Why the second time? Because the first time was under Moses.

He recovers the remnant “from Assyria”, modern-day Turkey, where you have the Afro-Turks; “and from Egypt”, lower Egypt and the Afro-Egyptians; “and from Pathros”, modern-day southern Sudan; “and from Cush”, Ethiopia; “and from Elam”, Iran and India, with the Afro-Iranians, the Siddis and the Dalits; “and from Shinar”, Iraq today and the Afro-Iraqis; “and from Hamath”, Syria today and the Afro-Syrians; “and from the islands of the sea”, like Cape Verde, the Hawaiian islands and the Melanesian islands.

“And he shall set up an ensign for the nations, and shall assemble the outcasts of Israel, and gather together the dispersed of Judah from the four corners of the earth.” We are the outcasts of Israel.

That is the all nations right there: the remnant of Israel gathered out of every land they were scattered to, the great multitude of Revelation 7:9.

precepts.text: The number of those sealed in the feast of the Lord who have fulfilled the law, then a great people on mount Zion whom Ezra could not number: Revelation 7:4 and 7:9 explained.
precepts.point: These are they which came out of great tribulation and washed their robes white in the blood of the Lamb: so much for not going through tribulation.

note.label: From Exile & Tribulation to Promise

precepts.why:
Revelation 7:4 gives “an hundred and forty and four thousand of all the tribes of the children of Israel”, and then verse 9 gives the great multitude. They say, see, we are all included. Ezra explains it crystal clear.

“Arise up and stand, behold the number of those that be sealed in the feast of the Lord”. That is Revelation 7:4, the 144,000. “Which are departed from the shadow of the world, and have received glorious garments of the Lord”: new bodies. “Take thy number, O Sion, and shut up those of thine that are clothed in white, which have fulfilled the law of the Lord. The number of thy children, whom thou longedst for, is fulfilled”. Verses 38 to 41 are Revelation 7:4.

Now verse 42: “I Esdras saw upon the mount Sion a great people, whom I could not number, and they all praised the Lord with songs.” That is Revelation 7:9. The great multitude is Zion, mount Zion.

So the 144,000 are the men, the Israelite leaders of the twelve tribes; the great multitude are more men, women and children of Israel. And “these are they which came out of great tribulation”: so much for the church teaching that we don’t have to go through tribulation.

precepts.text: Four angels hold the four winds, destruction, that they blow not on the earth (the armies), the sea (the navy), nor any tree (the air force), until another angel with the seal of the living God, which is the law of Isaiah 8:16, has sealed the servants of God: 144,000 of all the tribes of the children of Israel. Once they are sealed, the end comes, destruction upon destruction.
precepts.point: When ye see the abomination of desolation spoken of by Daniel stand in the holy place. Christ called the white man that, and the same people are in the land today.

note.label: Prophesy From Pain to Peace

precepts.why:
“And this gospel of the kingdom shall be preached in all the world for a witness unto all nations; and then shall the end come.” Some say that contradicts Isaiah 66, where the Lord gathers his people out of the nations. It does not. The world Christ speaks of here goes into the 144,000, and Revelation 7 shows it.

“I saw four angels standing on the four corners of the earth, holding the four winds of the earth, that the wind should not blow on the earth, nor on the sea, nor on any tree.” The four winds are destruction. The earth is the armies on land; the sea is the navy and the marines; any tree is the air force, which comes down above the trees.

“And I saw another angel ascending from the east, having the seal of the living God”. The seal of the living God is the law: “Bind up the testimony, seal the law among my disciples.” That is what the angel is looking for.

Verse three is the point that ties in with Matthew 24: “Hurt not the earth, neither the sea, nor the trees, till we have sealed the servants of our God in their foreheads.” Do not let the destruction come until the servants of God are sealed. “And there were sealed an hundred and forty and four thousand of all the tribes of the children of Israel.”

Once the 144,000 are sealed, then shall the end come: destruction upon destruction upon destruction. And because the 144,000 are scattered among the nations, the gospel must be preached among all the nations. That is why we must go out and prophesy and teach among all these different nations: our people are there.

precepts.text: A great multitude which no man could number, of all nations, kindreds, people, and tongues. Christians use this to confuse you. Acts 2:5 shows Jews, devout men out of every nation under heaven, and Tobit 13:3-4 says confess him before the Gentiles, ye children of Israel, for he hath scattered us among them. The multitude is Israelites out of every nation, and James wrote to the twelve tribes scattered abroad.
precepts.point: When thou art in tribulation and all these things are come upon thee, even in the latter days, if thou turn to the Lord and be obedient, he is a merciful God; he will not forsake thee nor destroy thee, the lake of fire, nor forget the covenant of thy fathers. That is the crown of life of Revelation 2:10.

note.label: Prophesy From Pain to Peace

precepts.why:
“After this I beheld, and, lo, a great multitude, which no man could number, of all nations, and kindreds, and people, and tongues, stood before the throne, and before the Lamb”. Christians go to Revelation 7:9 to try to confuse you. They say all people coming out of all nations means all peoples, every race, standing before the throne.

But Moses already told us who would be found in all nations: “the Lord shall scatter you among the nations, and ye shall be left few in number among the heathen”. That scattering was slavery, and we were left few in number because they were killing us. So a great multitude coming out of every nation and kindred and tongue is the scattered children of Israel, gathered back out of the lands they were taken to.

The precepts read right behind it settle it: Acts 2:5 shows Jews, devout men, “out of every nation under heaven”; Tobit 13 says “ye children of Israel: for he hath scattered us among them”; Ezekiel 28:25 speaks of the Lord gathering “the house of Israel from the people among whom they are scattered”; and James wrote “to the twelve tribes which are scattered abroad”. The multitude before the throne is Israel out of every nation. If they confound you with Revelation 7:9 on the street, shame on you.

precepts.text: Give him no rest, till he establish, and till he make Jerusalem a praise in the earth. That is what we do. But if we really wanted it, there is no way we would entertain sin under our noses while telling the Lord to hurry up. You might get slain.
precepts.point: The sea is the navy and the battleships; the trees burn when the fire comes; it is the same scene as 2 Esdras 13:5, the multitude gathered from the four winds to subdue the man from the sea. The nations will try to fight Christ to keep us in slavery, and he is coming to destroy every one of them, and us too if we are not right.

note.label: The Vantage Point of the Elders: the Fathers Have Spoken

precepts.why:
The four angels hold the four winds “that the wind should not blow on the earth, nor on the sea, nor on any tree”, and the cry goes out, “Hurt not the earth, neither the sea, nor the trees, till we have sealed the servants of our God in their foreheads.” So the question always comes: when are we getting out of here? By right, we want to get out. We pray every day, Lord, bring the destruction so we can leave.

Isaiah 62:7 is that prayer: “And give him no rest, till he establish, and till he make Jerusalem a praise in the earth.” That is what we are doing. We are not to give the Lord rest until he delivers us, establishes us and makes Jerusalem a praise in the earth.

But the question is, do we really want it? If we really wanted it, there would be no way we would be entertaining sin, no way we would allow evil right up under our noses while telling the Lord to hurry up. You mess around and you get slain.

The Lord has his timetable, and we are not on that level. You only see your own point of view; you do not have the Lord’s vantage point, looking at everything on this planet coming into the synchronicity he is waiting for. The angels are holding back whole armies until the sealing is finished, perhaps until that one last brother wakes up. You cannot push him. What you are responsible for is your own spirit and your own shenanigans. Get yourself right, and he will take care of the rest.

precepts.text: Make the time short, remember the covenant, and let them declare thy wonderful works. We say it, but we are not on the Lord's level; he will not be a millisecond late. In the meantime be in the right spiritual space so the day does not catch you as a thief. Examine yourselves, and examine your brothers and sisters; the ones who say they can fellowship at home do not want anyone to see their evil, and the wounds of a friend are better than the kisses of an enemy.
precepts.point: The sea is the navy and the battleships; the trees burn when the fire comes; it is the same scene as 2 Esdras 13:5, the multitude gathered from the four winds to subdue the man from the sea. The nations will try to fight Christ to keep us in slavery, and he is coming to destroy every one of them, and us too if we are not right.

note.label: The Vantage Point of the Elders: the Fathers Have Spoken

precepts.why:
Here is another thing we say: make the time short, “remember the covenant, and let them declare thy wonderful works.” Lord, make the time short; remember the covenant you made with us; let the nations know you love us, tear these nations up and set us on high.

But you are not on the Lord’s level. Believe me, the Lord will not be a millisecond late when it comes to sending his angels in to destroy our enemies, and you do not know that time. So in our wanting it, what should we be doing? Making sure we are in the right spiritual and mental space, so that when he sends the angels we are not caught off guard as by a thief in the night. We want to declare his wonderful works with a hundred percent confidence, not nervous that we are still in sin somewhere that has not been found out yet.

That is why the Bible says examine yourselves, whether ye be in the faith. Congregations have to examine themselves; examine your brothers and your sisters. The people who say, I don’t need to congregate, I can fellowship at home, say it because they don’t want anybody to see their nasty, wicked evil. When you come in here it is going to show, and righteous brothers and sisters are going to point it out.

Accept that correction, because it is love: the wounds of a friend rather than the kisses of an enemy. Somebody telling you where it is at will keep you out of trouble and set you right for when the Lord does send the angels. The angels are holding the four winds until the servants of God are sealed; make sure you are one of them when the time is made short.

precepts.text: A wind arose from the sea, that man waxed strong with the thousands of heaven, all things trembled at his look, and whensoever the voice went out of his mouth all they burned that heard it, as the earth faileth when it feeleth the fire. If Christ is coming back with that power he sees your hidden thoughts and actions. Then a multitude out of number from the four winds gathered to subdue him, the armies set to fight our deliverer.
precepts.point: The sea is the navy and the battleships; the trees burn when the fire comes; it is the same scene as 2 Esdras 13:5, the multitude gathered from the four winds to subdue the man from the sea. The nations will try to fight Christ to keep us in slavery, and he is coming to destroy every one of them, and us too if we are not right.

note.label: The Vantage Point of the Elders: the Fathers Have Spoken

precepts.why:
Visualize the scene of Revelation 7: four angels standing on the four corners of the earth, holding the four winds. That wind is not the regular wind that blows every day; it is destruction. The four corners are where the militaries are, straining to get at each other, ready to press the buttons, and the angels are holding them back. Bishop Nathanyel, who is an artist, once drew this scene.

2 Esdras 13 is the same scene. “There arose a wind from the sea, that it moved all the waves thereof. And I beheld, and, lo, that man waxed strong with the thousands of heaven: and when he turned his countenance to look, all the things trembled that were seen under him.” That is how Christ is coming back. “And whensoever the voice went out of his mouth, all they burned that heard his voice, like as the earth faileth when it feeleth the fire.” If Christ is coming back with that kind of power, you think he will not see your wicked thoughts and the things you thought you were hiding? You don’t want to be on the wrong side of that magnificent coming.

“And after this I beheld, and, lo, there was gathered together a multitude of men, out of number, from the four winds of the heaven, to subdue the man that came out of the sea”. The armies are setting up to fight against our deliverer. These nations do not want Christ to save us; they want us to remain in sin and evil so they can keep subduing and destroying the Israelites.

So the Lord tells the four angels, hold the four winds; don’t let them fight yet. When Christ comes back these armies will try to fight him to keep us in slavery, and he is coming to destroy every last one of them. And if we are not right, he is going to destroy us too. Brothers and sisters, make sure your diligence is on par.

precepts.text: The number of the sealed, an hundred and forty and four thousand of all the tribes of the children of Israel; the same company 2 Esdras 2 describes.
precepts.point: The sealed of the Lord receive the same. The hundred forty and four thousand of Revelation 7 that must be sealed before destruction comes are read of again in 2 Esdras: they departed from the shadow of the world, leaving spiritual Egypt and the ways Babylon taught behind, and have received glorious garments of the Lord. In the kingdom of heaven the Most High will clothe His men in glorious garments as in ancient times, on another level than anything worn today.

note.label: Exodus 28: Holy Garments for Glory and for Beauty

precepts.why:
“And I heard the number of them which were sealed: and there were sealed an hundred and forty and four thousand of all the tribes of the children of Israel.”

This is the number of those that be sealed that 2 Esdras 2 speaks of: the hundred forty and four thousand of all the tribes of the children of Israel, who must be sealed before destruction comes. They are the same company that departed from the shadow of the world and received glorious garments of the Lord, the garments of glory and beauty first given to Aaron and his sons.

precepts.text: When the tribes are sealed, Dan is not named among them; the tribe that set up the graven image never rose up again.
precepts.point: Hear the word against Dan by the prophet: they that swear by the sin of Samaria and say, thy god, O Dan, liveth, shall fall and never rise up again. Mind you, it is an idol made with hands, yet they called it living. That is why Dan has no gate among the sealed tribes in Revelation 7; Dan was discontinued as a tribe of itself and intertwined with Benjamin for the most part.

note.label: Judges 18: Dan Steals Micah's Gods and Takes Laish

precepts.why:
When the tribes are sealed, Dan is not named among them: Juda, Reuben, Gad, Aser, Nepthalim, Manasses, Simeon, Levi, Issachar, Zabulon, Joseph and Benjamin, twelve thousand of each, and no Dan. The tribe that set up the graven image the first thing in its land, and kept an idol from Micah’s day to Jeroboam’s, fell and never rose up again, as Amos said.

That is why Dan has no gate among the sealed tribes in Revelation 7. Dan was discontinued as a tribe of itself and intertwined with Benjamin for the most part.

precepts.text: Twelve thousand are sealed of each tribe, but Dan is missing, because Dan fell and was absorbed.
precepts.point: Jeroboam sealed the split with idolatry, making two golden calves in Bethel and Dan, ordaining a feast of his own in the eighth month, and setting up priests of the lowest people, so the northern kingdom sank deeper and deeper into idol worship. Dan fell so hard that the tribe was absorbed and left out of the sealed tribes.

note.label: Acts 10: Cornelius and the Northern Kingdom Grafted In

precepts.why:
“And I heard the number of them which were sealed: and there were sealed an hundred and forty and four thousand of all the tribes of the children of Israel.” Twelve thousand are sealed of each tribe: Juda, Reuben, Gad, Aser, Nepthalim, Manasses, Simeon, Levi, Issachar, Zabulon, Joseph and Benjamin.

Dan is missing. Dan fell into the idolatry of the golden calf and was absorbed, and so Dan is left out of the sealed tribes. That is how deep the northern kingdom's idolatry went.

note.label: The Gospel Is Black Liberation

precepts.why:
